newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: North says Robe iron ore output hits peak.
newsitem.headline: North says Robe iron ore output hits peak.

text.p: Western Australian iron ore miner Robe River posted a series of production and shipping records in May following its record output in the 1996/97 ore year ended March 31, operator North Ltd said on Tuesday.

The month included a week during which Robe achieved a sustained rate of shiploading equivalent to 50 million tonnes a year, compared with annual shiploading capacity of 32 million tonnes, North said.
The feat occurred as Robe River cleared a sudden build up of vessels off the loading port of Cape Lambert, it said.

Of the total 2.63 million tonnes shipped from Cape Lambert in May, 967,528 tonnes was loaded in a single week, about 90,000 tonnes better than the previous weekly record, set four years ago, North said.
Robe also set a new daily shiploading mark of 166,270 tonnes and a record 24 hour average shiploading rate of 6,815 tonnes per hour from its single shiploader.

Production into its Cape Lambert stockpiles in May totalled 2.75 million tonnes of sinter fines and lump, an annualised rate of 33 million tonnes, which compares with annual plant capacity of 28 million tonnes.

Robe's 1996/97 record production was 27.5 million tonnes, some 142,000 tonnes better than its previous record, established in 1995/96, supporting its position as the world's fourth largest seaborne trader in iron ore, North said.
North holds a 65 percent stake, including 12 percent attributable to minorities, in Robe River Iron Ore Associates.
Other shareholders are subsidiaries of Mitsui & Co Ltd, Sumitomo Corp and Nippon Steel Corp.
